name: Split
tagline: A 1,700-year-old Roman emperor's palace that never stopped being a living city, its ancient walls now filled with homes, cafés and a cathedral built from his own mausoleum.
highlight: Sitting for a coffee in the Peristyle at dusk, Roman columns and a sphinx from Luxor lit up exactly where Diocletian once held court.
shortDescription: A 1,700-year-old Roman emperor's palace that never stopped being a living city, Croatia's second city and the main gateway to the Dalmatian islands.
metaDescription: A Split travel guide: Diocletian's Palace, the Peristyle, the Riva promenade, Marjan Hill, food and how to plan a visit to Croatia's Dalmatian hub.
knownFor: Diocletian's Palace, the Riva promenade, Marjan Hill
intro: Split is genuinely built around one of the most unusual historic sites in Europe, a Roman emperor's retirement palace that never stopped being lived in for the 1,700 years since.
Diocletian's Palace's ancient walls now genuinely enclose an entire working neighbourhood — homes, shops, cafés and a cathedral converted from the emperor's own mausoleum.
Beyond the palace, Split is genuinely Croatia's second city and busiest ferry hub, with its own beaches, a green hillside park and a lively waterfront promenade.

whyVisit.intro: Split's case rests genuinely on a Roman palace that's stayed a real, living city for nearly two millennia.

points.title: Diocletian's Palace is genuinely unlike anywhere else
points.text: A 1,700-year-old Roman palace still functioning as an actual, lived-in neighbourhood.

points.title: It's genuinely a real Croatian city, not just a resort
points.text: A working port and Dalmatia's largest city, with an authentic, year-round pulse.

points.title: The Riva promenade is genuinely a proper daily ritual
points.text: Palm-lined waterfront cafés where locals and visitors alike watch the harbour.

points.title: Marjan Hill offers genuinely excellent nature right in the city
points.text: Forested trails and viewpoints a short walk from the historic centre.

points.title: It's genuinely the best base for island-hopping
points.text: Croatia's busiest ferry port, with frequent connections to Hvar, Brač and beyond.

attractionsIntro: Split's essential sights are genuinely concentrated within and around the ancient walls of Diocletian's Palace.

attractions.name: Diocletian's Palace
attractions.text: Genuinely a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a living neighbourhood at once, a Roman emperor's palace still filled with homes and shops today.
attractions.tip: Genuinely get lost in the palace's narrow side streets — the real character lives away from the main routes.

attractions.name: The Peristyle

image.alt: The Peristyle at Diocletian's Palace in Split, with an ancient Egyptian sphinx

attractions.text: Genuinely the palace's ceremonial heart, a sunken Roman courtyard still ringed by columns and a genuine Egyptian sphinx.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit in the evening, when café tables fill the square and it feels properly alive.

attractions.name: The Cathedral of St Domnius

image.alt: The Cathedral of St Domnius in Split

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the oldest Catholic cathedrals in the world still in its original structure — Diocletian's own mausoleum, repurposed.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb the bell tower for the best rooftop view over the whole palace and harbour.

attractions.name: The Riva waterfront promenade

image.alt: The palm-lined Riva promenade in Split

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's social stage, a palm-lined seafront promenade right outside the palace's southern wall.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a lovely spot for a slow evening coffee or aperitivo.

attractions.name: Marjan Hill
attractions.text: Genuinely a forested peninsula park right beside the city centre, with trails, chapels and sweeping sea views.
attractions.tip: Genuinely go for sunset — the views over Split and the islands are genuinely spectacular.

attractions.name: The Golden Gate and Gregory of Nin statue

image.file: File:Gregory of Nin statue in Split, Croatia (48693918937).jpg
image.alt: The statue of Gregory of Nin near Split's Golden Gate

attractions.text: Genuinely the palace's grandest original entrance, guarded outside by Ivan Meštrović's towering bronze statue.
attractions.tip: Genuinely rub the statue's toe — a well-known local tradition said to bring good luck.

attractions.name: Bačvice Beach
attractions.text: Genuinely the city's most popular beach, a shallow sandy bay a short walk from the historic centre.
attractions.tip: Genuinely watch for a game of picigin, the local beach sport invented right here.

thingsToDoIntro: Split genuinely rewards splitting time between its ancient palace streets and its very real, modern city life.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Diocletian's Palace's ancient streets
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential experience, getting lost among the palace's Roman substructure and centuries of later additions.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit the palace's atmospheric underground cellars, among the best-preserved Roman substructures anywhere.

thingsToDo.title: Climb the Cathedral bell tower

image.alt: Climbing the bell tower of Split's Cathedral of St Domnius

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding, if slightly precarious, climb, with the palace's best rooftop view waiting at the top.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely not for the faint of heart — the stairs are steep and narrow in places.

thingsToDo.title: Rub Gregory of Nin's toe for luck

image.alt: The statue of Gregory of Nin outside Split's Golden Gate

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fun, low-key local tradition, joining the line of visitors polishing the statue's bronze big toe.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely an easy stop combined with the Golden Gate itself.

thingsToDo.title: Hike or bike Marjan Hill

image.alt: A hiking trail on Marjan Hill above Split

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely refreshing break from the historic centre, trails winding through pine forest to several viewpoints.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bring water — shade is limited once you're above the tree line at the top.

thingsToDo.title: Swim and watch picigin at Bačvice Beach

image.file: File:Aerial view of Bacvice Beach in Split, Croatia (48608745867).jpg
image.alt: Bačvice Beach in Split from above

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely lively city beach scene, complete with the locally invented ball game picigin played in the shallows.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a short walk from the palace — an easy way to cool off between sightseeing.

thingsToDo.title: Stroll the Riva promenade at sunset

image.alt: Sunset on the Riva promenade in Split

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential evening ritual, joining locals and visitors alike for a slow walk along the palm-lined waterfront.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a great spot to watch the ferries come and go while the light fades.

foodIntro: Split's food genuinely means classic Dalmatian cooking, with a regional pie worth seeking out beyond the seafood staples.

foods.name: Fresh grilled seafood

image.alt: Grilled seafood at a traditional Croatian konoba

foods.text: Genuinely a highlight of dining here, fish and shellfish grilled simply at konobas throughout the palace.
foods.whereToTry: Konobas throughout Diocletian's Palace and the wider old town.

foods.name: Crni rižot (black risotto)

image.alt: Black risotto made with cuttlefish ink

foods.text: Genuinely a Dalmatian classic worth trying at least once during a Split visit.
foods.whereToTry: Seafood restaurants throughout the old town.

foods.name: Dalmatinski pršut (dry-cured ham)
foods.text: Genuinely a reliable starter, often served with local cheese and olives.

foods.name: Soparnik (savoury Swiss chard pie)
foods.text: Genuinely a distinctive regional specialty from the Poljica area just outside Split, a thin pie filled with chard and baked under embers.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional bakeries and markets, especially the Split Green Market.

foods.name: Croatian wine
foods.text: Genuinely worth exploring, with Dalmatian reds from nearby Pelješac and Hvar both widely available.
foods.whereToTry: Wine bars throughout the old town.

foods.name: Fritule (small fried doughnuts)
foods.text: Genuinely a nice sweet treat, found at bakeries and market stalls around the old town.

accommodation.intro: Split genuinely offers accommodation for every budget, with location inside or outside the palace walls making a real difference.

areas.text: The most atmospheric base, staying inside the ancient walls themselves.

areas.name: Varoš or the Riva area

areas.text: An easy walk from the centre, with a more local, residential feel.

gettingThere.intro: Split is genuinely Croatia's busiest transport hub after Zagreb, well connected by air, road and sea.

options.text: Genuinely available from many European cities, especially in summer.
options.detail: Split Airport sits about 25 minutes from the city centre.

options.text: Genuinely a comfortable, scenic option along the coast.
options.detail: Takes around five to six hours from Zagreb, or four to five from Dubrovnik.

options.text: Genuinely the main gateway for island-hopping around Dalmatia.
options.detail: Frequent connections to Hvar, Brač, Korčula and beyond.

gettingAround.intro: Split's genuinely compact old town is entirely walkable, with buses covering the wider city and Marjan Hill.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to explore Diocletian's Palace itself.
options.detail: No cars are permitted within the ancient palace walls.

options.text: Genuinely useful for reaching Marjan Hill's far side or outlying neighbourhoods.
options.detail: A frequent, inexpensive network across the wider city.

options.text: Genuinely conveniently located right beside the old town.
options.detail: Both sit an easy walk from most central accommodation.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for warm weather without peak-summer crowds
bestTime.summary: Split is genuinely busiest in July and August, with shoulder months offering a much better balance of weather and crowds.

seasons.text: Genuinely warm enough to swim, with noticeably thinner crowds than peak summer.
Genuinely hot and lively, the busiest season for both the city and its ferry connections.
Genuinely still warm enough for the beach, with crowds and prices both easing off.
Genuinely quiet, with a real, lived-in city atmosphere rather than a tourist-focused one.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely nothing strongly, though peak July and August bring the heaviest crowds to the palace and ferry terminals alike.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Split visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely ferry tickets ahead in peak summer if you're continuing on to the islands.
Climb genuinely the Cathedral bell tower for the best view over the whole palace.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes — the palace's ancient streets are cobbled and can be slippery.
Visit genuinely Marjan Hill in the late afternoon for the best light and cooler temperatures.
Try genuinely soparnik at the Green Market for a taste of the wider Split region.
Use genuinely Split as a base for day trips to Krka National Park or the nearby islands.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Split?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers the palace, Marjan Hill and the beach at a comfortable pace.

faq.q: Is Diocletian's Palace still lived in?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — around 3,000 people still live and work within the ancient palace walls today.

faq.q: Is Split a good base for island-hopping?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's Croatia's busiest ferry port, with frequent connections to Hvar, Brač, Korčula and beyond.

faq.q: How do you get from Split Airport to the city centre?
faq.a: Genuinely by airport shuttle bus or taxi, taking about 25 to 30 minutes.

faq.q: Is Split worth visiting versus just Dubrovnik?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the two offer quite different experiences, and Split's living Roman palace is genuinely unlike anywhere else.
Yes, genuinely — Bačvice Beach sits a short walk from the palace, with more beaches further along Marjan Hill.
